b: I am an engineering student, so far throughout university I've always been someone that skipped lectures to do shit on their own time/because I can self-study a lot faster. IMO this was a complete blunder on my part. I did get very good grades in SOME courses, but for others due to a lack of self-motivation/poor time management I did way worse than I expected.

This was very disheartening for me, because I am actually a successful engineer outside the classroom. I do great work on design teams and on my personal projects, and I got a very good internship as a freshman. I was really successful in high school both academically and in robotics competitions (I got my team to Worlds) but I kept feeling like I would always miss the mark by just a bit academically, mostly due to not having enough time to study everything, and I'd vow to do better next term and the cycle would just keep repeating.

Going to lectures has fixed this for me, I don't even really try too hard to pay attention or keep track of what is going on, because like I said I'm good at self-studying. The reason it works is this.
1) Having to go forces me to maintain a calibrated sleep schedule and structure in my life, this alone makes me way more productive. I took this further and ended up scheduling my week.
2) You stop feeling like a bum because being in the lecture hall alone makes you feel somewhat productive even if you are doing something completely unrelated on your computer.

3) If you are significantly behind on course content, realizing you have no clue wtf is going on while listening to the lecture motivates you to actually go study ASAP and catch up/go even further and just finish the course content instead of just putting it off.

You are almost certainly not using the extra time you get from skipping lectures effectively (atleast I wasn't), so you might as well go. Worst-case scenario, you will feel somewhat more productive and feel more in control of your life.
